Verb rendered be laid waste. This is a light verb plus complement, not a verb plus phrasal particle: by the subtraction of rules 44 and 31, be laid alone names no ruin while waste carries the lexeme of נָצָה, so the head is t036. Rule 44 expressly forbids reading rule 24's lexical predicate over auxiliaries as a preference for the English verb, which is the competing reading that would head on laid.
מֵאֵין fused into the single English word without, rule 30; head on the negation, which is what the word carries.
Anarthrous participle rendered inhabitant; the ASV supplies no noun phrase for it, so rule 46 adds nothing to the unit.

review_notes: Twenty-five source and thirty-eight target tokens partitioned exactly once.

Corrected: the target head of s022 תִּצֶּינָה moves from t035 laid to t036 waste. be laid waste is a light verb plus complement under rule 44, and waste is the word whose loss loses the lexeme; the accepted unit had cited rule 24, which rule 44 says must not be read as a preference for the English verb.
The two other judgment calls stand and are argued in place: the idiom he is on his way for נָסַע, and t031 that as a supplied subordinator under rule 55.
